_doc: run_regression.py's MEASURED time table (spec S4-1). `suites`: wall seconds of each suite run alone, from the recon note 2026-10-21-A2-P7-recon.md Q1 (the quiet run 2026-10-21-kb1-fix-units.txt for the units; date line to mtime for the reverts; revert_safety_gates and revert_step5 the larger of their two runs (revert_step5 REPLACED 2026-10-31 by 3460 s, measured alone on 131b7ec5 with 425 mutants (OVERALL PASS), after the full lanes on a869af0c and 54ce416d both timed out at the 3600 s floor that the stale 237 s left it); revert_r1 its full run alone, 1166.9 s with 514 mutants, measured 2026-10-29 by the R1 + R2 follow-up's second fix round (review RV-4: the 917 it replaced was below both measured runs; the full lane's run on f4412116, 468 mutants, took 1153.7 s)). They order the work longest-first (revert_step3 starts FIRST: it is the wall floor) and give a suite whose TIMEOUT_FACTOR (3.5x since the S4-1 fix round: the first real --full run took 4,339 s for revert_step3, 86 % of 2.5x) exceeds the default timeout a longer one. `test_check_purity`: each test method run alone and serially, measured 2026-10-21 by the S4-1 builder (sum 260.5 s, the recon's 265 s quiet); it balances the shards. A method missing here (a new test) is planned at `default_method_s` and still runs: the planner names the tests unittest's own loader collects from the module (`loader_names`), never this table. revert_bossprep and revert_p11 (the chapter 6-7 merge, 2026-11-13): PROVISIONAL rows, (mutants + 1) x the seconds one run took in the closing pass's full mutant runs under load; upper bounds until measured alone. revert_step5, revert_r1, revert_step3 and revert_safety_gates (the same merge, 2026-11-13, before its full lane): RAISED to the seconds the side branches' own full lanes measured, because the old rows put their caps at or under those lanes' times: the 2026-11-11 lane on c5146e53 killed revert_step5, revert_r1 and revert_step3 at their caps (12110, 4084.5 and 7049 s: lower bounds) and ran revert_safety_gates 3455.6 s (96 % of its 3600 s floor); the 2026-11-09 lane on dd8b31ef ran revert_step5 12004.5 s with 686 mutants (704 now) and revert_r1 2936.2 s; upper bounds under load until measured alone. The chapter 6-7 merge's full lane (2026-11-14, on fa9f073d: `REGRESSION: PASS (full, 41 suites, 14363.9 s wall)`, 07 2026-11-14), run beside the bot tuner's 12 lanes, measured the 19 rows written in A1's first code commit, each that suite's seconds in `ai_player/evidence/2026-11-14-regression-*` rounded up (loaded times, not alone): ten NEW (test_live_chain, test_kb2, test_ways, test_bossprep, test_step53_a1, test_live_ki128, test_step53_rs, test_measure_step5, check_grader_imports, test_step53_a2) and nine RAISED (test_host, test_eyes, test_evidence, test_goals, test_safety_gates, check_fairness, check_lessons, revert_step11, revert_step4); and revert_step5 RAISED from 12110 to 14363, its 14,362.8 s in that lane (703 mutants). revert_frontier (A1, 2026-11-14; the lead's call: it joins the full lane): ceil(1.2 x its SERIAL time), 1.2 x 5045 s -> 6054, because the lane runs it with no --workers (serial, its default); measured ONCE on 2026-11-15 (2:22 AM to 3:46 AM) beside the bot tuner's 12 lanes and no other A1 job (`revert_frontier.py` with no arguments, its control and 222 mutants, `OVERALL: PASS`), on the working tree just before the commit of the verifier's round-4 fix (the round-3 fix's 218 mutants had measured 4866 s -> 5840, the round-2 fix's 135 mutants 2509 s -> 3011, the round-1 fix's 126 mutants 2260 s -> 2712, B3's 106 mutants 1821 s -> 2186): one measurement, not an alone-time.
